workerObjectives.objective: Inventory every optional or experimental agentic mechanism and trace its entry points through configuration, CLI/API wiring, feature flags, and runtime orchestration. For each mechanism, determine who decides to activate/adopt it and whether it is default, opt-in, or conditional; cite repository paths and explicitly record mechanisms or paths that remain uncertain or unexamined.
workerObjectives.scopeHint: Focus on startup/entrypoint code, configuration schemas, CLI/API surfaces, feature flags, and orchestration dispatch. Do not primarily assess detailed tool authority or persistence implementation.

workerObjectives.objective: For each mechanism identified in the harness, audit the agent's effective capabilities and authority boundary: tools, filesystem/network/process access, delegation rights, approval gates, and what artifact/evidence it returns to the outer harness. Determine who can accept or reject the result and cite the implementation, schemas, and result-handling paths; preserve ambiguities and incomplete coverage.
workerObjectives.scopeHint: Focus on agent construction, tool registries, permissions/policies, approval/adoption logic, result/artifact contracts, and outer-harness consumption. Avoid duplicating feature-activation inventory except where needed to identify mechanisms.

workerObjectives.objective: Assess whether each optional or experimental agentic mechanism has durable execution and what lifecycle guarantees exist across retries, crashes, restarts, resumptions, checkpoints, and persisted artifacts. Trace persistence, scheduling, recovery, and test/documentation evidence, and relate findings to the remaining authority of the outer harness. Clearly distinguish implemented support, conditional support, absent support, and unknowns with repository-path citations.
workerObjectives.scopeHint: Focus on execution lifecycle, queues/runners, state stores, checkpoints, retry/recovery code, persistence formats, and tests/docs proving durability. Do not re-audit tool inventories or activation configuration unless needed to establish lifecycle scope.

variant.coverageSummary: All three child investigations succeeded, so there are no failed-child omissions. The synthesis covers the identified optional and experimental mechanisms, their entry/adoption gates, capabilities, returned artifacts, outer-harness authority, defaults, and lifecycle support. Coverage is nevertheless incomplete at several implementation edges: exact CLI dispatch, full execution-branch ordering, every durable/delivery caller, complete tool-result assembly, and crash behavior around in-flight model/tool/external side effects remain uncertain as documented above.

report.objective: Inventory every optional or experimental agentic mechanism and trace its entry points through configuration, CLI/API wiring, feature flags, and runtime orchestration. For each mechanism, determine who decides to activate/adopt it and whether it is default, opt-in, or conditional; cite repository paths and explicitly record mechanisms or paths that remain uncertain or unexamined.

findings.claim: Normal CLI startup is a single manual task entrypoint (`--task` or stdin), loads env-backed config, and invokes `runV1Harness` with `contextMode: "variant"`; no experimental capability is enabled there. Config requires OPENAI_API_KEY and OPENAI_MODEL, with optional OPENAI_REPAIR_MODEL and fixed budgets/paths.

The main orchestration API exposes opt-in seams for planning, Worker subagents, MCP repository reads, A2A delegation, verified memory, advisory ReviewPlan/decomposed units, bounded fan-out, admitted Spec, and durability. Each is represented as an optional runV1Harness option, while comments explicitly label the first several experiment-only and state defaults remain off/in-memory.

Explicit Planner is opt-in/conditional: `planningEnabled` is checked by `shouldRunPlanner(planningEnabled)`, and the experiment compares baseline Spec→Worker against a variant with a read-only Planner. The experiment encodes `defaultUnchanged: true`; Plan is advisory and cannot expand Spec/authorize edits. The architecture experiment conclusion is therefore an adoption candidate only via measured experiment, not automatic activation.

Bounded research Subagent is opt-in: `shouldEnableSubagents` only returns true for an explicit true flag; only implementation episodes receive `delegate_research`, with MAX_RESEARCH_DELEGATIONS=1 and a read-only EvidenceReport contract. Evidence is advisory, not Spec/permission/success. The experiment explicitly says unused optional delegation is evidence and Subagents are not made default.

MCP repo_read_file is opt-in and restricted to implementation: runBenchmark passes the boolean option through, runAgentLoop requires the flag plus implementation phase, opens/admit-checks a session, removes direct read_file, and records admission. The standalone MCP probe activates it explicitly and checks direct reads are absent; repair/review remain direct-tool paths.

A2A remote impact analysis is opt-in, implementation-only, and bounded to one delegation. The standalone A2A probe refuses to run unless A2A_REMOTE_OPENAI_API_KEY is set (no fallback), then explicitly passes a2aDelegationEnabled flag. Remote artifact acceptance does not grant workflow success; final VERIFY/REVIEW still decide outcome.

Conversation continuation via `previous_response_id` is an experimental selectable orchestration mode; runAgentLoop defaults to manual history replay, while the experiment runs manual and previous_response_id arms and evaluates chain/replay evidence. Architecture documents it as experimental with default manual and no established economic improvement.

Verified repository memory is opt-in: MemoryRunOptions requires a storeDir and has independent promote/retrieve switches; normal runV1Harness defaults to no read/write. Retrieval is repository-scoped and revalidates records before injecting an advisory hint; promotion requires supported verification/review evidence. Memory cannot change WorkflowState per the run API comments/architecture.

Human-reviewable decomposition is conditional/opt-in rather than default. A harness-bound ReviewPlan can split work into sequential UnitExecutionScope episodes with dependencies and cumulative verification; ReviewPlan is advisory while UnitExecutionScope is harness process control. The corrected experiment says default remains Spec→one Worker and adoption is pending human-review evidence.

Bounded parallel fan-out is opt-in/experimental: it executes frozen plan units in sequential or Promise.all parallel schedules, exact-base workspaces, child verification, and deterministic Git fan-in. The experiment's predeclared rule requires correctness, all gates, no conflicts/lost changes, >=20% full end-to-end wall improvement, and no >20% cost regression; it explicitly preserves one Worker as default.

Durable checkpoints are opt-in: `durable` absent means current in-memory workflow; when present the outer runner acquires a lease and uses WorkflowState phases spec_required→implementation_ready→review_ready→terminal with harness-admitted transitions. Durable state can resume without rerunning earlier phases, but does not provide mid-Worker crash reconciliation/exactly-once semantics (documented limitation).

Post-terminal GitHub delivery is a separate opt-in orchestration path, not part of runV1Harness. `runDelivery` requires a terminal successful WorkflowState, acquires a lease, fresh local VERIFY, then progresses local acceptance→branch/PR→CI and at most one repair; it explicitly has no merge authority and GitHub is not fenced by WorkflowState.

Durable independent REVIEW retry is harness-controlled and conditional on failure classification/budget rather than model choice. `decideRetry` stops permanent/semantic failures, requests reconciliation for ambiguous side effects, and retries otherwise until max attempts; the model neither classifies nor budgets. Default max review retry attempts is 2, and retry state is part of review_ready durable state.

Repair model routing is an optional configuration mechanism: all episodes use OPENAI_MODEL unless the episode is verification repair and OPENAI_REPAIR_MODEL is nonempty; this is a conditional override, not a general agent-selection policy. `withPinnedModel` is an additional benchmark/qualification pin that rejects nested pins.

Skills are phase-selected procedural context rather than a user-facing feature flag: runAgentLoop selects a phase skill and injects it when available. The architecture lists one evidence-guided repair Skill as retained core, so this is not classified as optional agentic orchestration, but its load is conditional on phase/skill availability.

uncertainties: The bottom-level CLI dispatch in run-benchmark.ts was not directly examinable because repository reads truncate the large file; package scripts prove named probe/experiment entrypoints exist, but exact flag-to-callback dispatch was not traced line-by-line.

I did not inspect every experimental probe/experiment module (routing, durability/checkpoint/ownership/CI probes, eval qualification) or all call sites that construct durable/delivery options. Findings cover their central APIs and documented architecture, but exact activation flags for those runner modes remain unexamined.

I did not inspect the full executeV1Harness body in run.ts, so the precise order in which memory, review-plan, fan-out, and durable dispatch branches are selected is inferred from the public option types, central loop behavior, and supporting modules rather than fully traced.

report.objective: For each mechanism identified in the harness, audit the agent's effective capabilities and authority boundary: tools, filesystem/network/process access, delegation rights, approval gates, and what artifact/evidence it returns to the outer harness. Determine who can accept or reject the result and cite the implementation, schemas, and result-handling paths; preserve ambiguities and incomplete coverage.

findings.claim: The default Worker receives four host-mediated tools: list_files/read_file over target-app, write_file constrained by resolveWithin to target-app/src, and run_command constrained exactly to npm test. npm test executes with a positive environment allowlist, but the verification process is not a general filesystem/network sandbox.

Agent episode success is deliberately weaker than workflow success: AgentRunResult.status means only that the model produced a terminal response, while the outer harness owns verification and workflow completion. The loop records changed files/diffs, discovery, token usage, tool calls, and delegation records for outer consumption.

Research delegation is opt-in and implementation-only, capped at one delegation and a six-turn child budget. The child can only list/read target-app files and submit EvidenceReport; it cannot write, run commands, delegate further, alter Spec, grant permission, or declare success. Reports are accepted only when cited evidence paths were actually read, and are explicitly advisory rather than authority, permission, verification, or workflow success.

The implementation Worker can optionally use MCP repo_read_file instead of direct read_file. Host admission pins protocol revision, admits only an allowlisted tool whose schema is strict and exposes no root/credential/token fields, and the server receives an absolute host-selected root while refusing to start if OPENAI_API_KEY is present. Writes and npm test remain direct harness tools.

The optional A2A mechanism is a single bounded implementation delegation. The model may provide only objective and scope; host code chooses local endpoint, allowed root, model, credentials, and protocol policy. Scope is resolved within target-app, remote process environment is allowlisted and receives only the remote key plus bounded configuration, and the remote executor is read-only (list/read/structured submit; no writes, shell, verification, review, or workflow decision).

A2A has explicit admission and artifact acceptance gates: the host validates agent name, advertised skill, HTTP+JSON interface URL, and compatible 1.0 protocol; it refuses to send on discovery/admission/client failures. A task must complete, then the ImpactAnalysis artifact must have in-scope bounded paths/findings. Accepted output is advisory evidence only and the immutable record grantsWorkflowSuccess is false.

Independent REVIEW is downstream authority over implementation quality, but only after deterministic VERIFY passes. Findings are parsed and classified by the harness against resolved Spec, changed-file scope, evidence/actionability, severity/confidence; accepted blocking findings trigger bounded repair, while no accepted blockers is review success. The model's own terminal response is not acceptance.

Repair decisions are harness-owned: verification pass ends repair; otherwise repeated unchanged failures or configured attempt ceilings stop, and only then does the workflow proceed/fail. Delivery acceptance requires local VERIFY pass and independent REVIEW pass before expectedHeadSha can advance.

CI evidence is classified by current expected head SHA; stale observations are ignored, infrastructure failures reobserved, policy failures permanently fail, and semantic failures allow at most one repair. A successful current-head CI observation yields ready_for_human_review rather than auto-merge authority.

The delivery artifact is intentionally a draft PR and explicitly says ready for human review and must not be auto-merged. Remote branch reconciliation refuses unexpected remote movement and draft PR reconciliation avoids duplicate open PRs; therefore human review/merge remains the ultimate external acceptance gate.

uncertainties: The read of loop.ts was truncated before the full executeWorkerTool and final result assembly; exact per-tool handling details beyond the visible construction and result type should be verified by a complete read if needed.

I did not inspect every outer run.ts state transition or all delivery-store persistence paths, so this report covers the visible agent/result contracts and acceptance functions but not every serialization consumer.
MCP's underlying child process can technically access whatever the host OS permits under its configured root; the application-level boundary is target-app plus path validation, not an OS sandbox.
A2A remote process uses the host target-app root and read guards, but the repository does not establish an independent OS/container isolation boundary.

report.objective: Assess whether each optional or experimental agentic mechanism has durable execution and what lifecycle guarantees exist across retries, crashes, restarts, resumptions, checkpoints, and persisted artifacts. Trace persistence, scheduling, recovery, and test/documentation evidence, and relate findings to the remaining authority of the outer harness. Clearly distinguish implemented support, conditional support, absent support, and unknowns with repository-path citations.

findings.claim: Durable workflow execution is implemented conditionally (opt-in durable mode), with file-backed WorkflowState phases spec_required, implementation_ready, review_ready, and terminal; transitions are schema-validated, atomically replaced via temp-file rename, and fresh invocations dispatch from the persisted phase rather than rerunning completed phases.

DUR01 proves interruption after implementation_ready can resume in a fresh process with same workflow/workspace/base provenance, Spec skipped, and Worker→VERIFY→REVIEW authority retained; terminal state is checked as persisted. This is probe support, not default normal in-memory behavior.

Checkpoint/resume at review_ready is implemented conditionally: a separately persisted, atomically written and fingerprint-checked FileSnapshot baseline is restored, workspace fingerprint is revalidated, and fresh process reconstruction skips Worker/pre-review VERIFY while running independent REVIEW. Tests cover missing/tampered baseline and workspace mutation fail-closed behavior.

Durable REVIEW retry is implemented conditionally, not as general exactly-once execution. Retry state (operationId, attempt count, budget, failure class) is persisted on review_ready before attempts; transient failures may be admitted by harness policy, and a fresh process can continue the same logical operation. Semantic, policy, unknown model errors, and ambiguous Worker side effects stop or require reconciliation; Worker/VERIFY retries are not crash-safe.

Single-machine ownership/fencing is implemented for durable WorkflowState and delivery state: leases persist owner/fencing token/expiry, saves validate ownership and expiry, and O_EXCL mutexes serialize file operations. Guarantees are bounded: expiry does not stop old processes, lock files can remain after crash and require manual recovery, no CAS/stateVersion, distributed scheduler, or cross-machine election exists.

Post-terminal GitHub delivery is an implemented optional durable lifecycle separate from WorkflowState. DeliveryState persists local acceptance, committed/published head, branch/PR reconciliation, CI waiting/observations, bounded one-time semantic CI repair, ready_for_human_review, or delivery_failed; runDelivery reloads existing state and reconciles deterministic branch/PR/expected head after restart, with fenced local state writes.

GitHub delivery is explicitly not exactly-once: WorkflowState fencing does not fence GitHub, external check→action races remain, remote reconciliation/no-force-push/expected-head checks are mitigations, and merged PRs are never treated as authority to merge. Remote side effects can require reconciliation.

Verified repository memory has durable file-backed persistence and restart retrieval: admitted records are validated, immutable against rewrite, scoped to repository, and stale claims rejected before injection. Durable workflow execution explicitly rejects memory retrieval/promotion, so memory is a separate optional artifact mechanism and cannot participate in durable resume state.

Bounded fan-out has runtime scheduling and workspace/source-delta artifacts, but no durable queue, child checkpoint, restart/resume protocol, or persisted child execution state. Sequential/parallel scheduling awaits children and deterministic fan-in detects conflicts/lost changes within one invocation; crash/restart support is absent.

Planner, subagent delegation, and conversation-state orchestration are experimental runtime mechanisms whose outputs are reports/traces, not durable workflow checkpoints. Experiment code writes reports and copies trial traces; architecture keeps Planner and bounded research subagent off by default. No persisted child queue or restart ownership is implemented. previous_response_id is provider continuation within an episode, not crash/restart durability.

The outer harness retains authority over workflow consequence: models do not mutate WorkflowState or decide retry admission; durable transitions, workspace binding, verification/review gates, retry budget, leases/fencing, delivery phase, and terminal outcomes are harness-owned. Trace JSONL and experiment artifacts are evidentiary rather than authoritative state.

uncertainties: No production crash-injection test was found for mid-Worker, mid-VERIFY, file rename, or an external GitHub side effect; those windows remain unsupported or require reconciliation.
Fan-out, Planner, subagent, and orchestration conclusions rely on inspected runtime experiment code/tests/docs; no durable-run adapter was found.
Filesystem atomic rename and lease/mutex behavior are application-level guarantees, not proven against power loss or network filesystems.
